rationale: Jesus introduces this quotation with "It is also written" (4:7) and quotes Deuteronomy 6:16 directly. Checked against both texts as shipped in this app, Matthew's quotation reproduces the command itself ("Do not put the Lord your God to the test" / "Do not test the LORD your God") but does not reproduce Deuteronomy's own closing clause naming the precedent for the command, "as you tested Him at Massah" -- the specific wilderness incident (Exodus 17:1-7) that gave the command its original occasion. The label stays explicit because the citation formula and the command itself are both unambiguous; the un-quoted clause is a difference in how much of the source verse is reproduced, not a difference in what the reproduced portion says.
